course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

lesson.title: Inverses of Exponential Functions
lesson.summary: The general form of a logarithmic function, how logarithmic growth reverses exponential growth, log_b x and bˣ as inverse functions, and reflecting graphs and ordered pairs over y = x.
learningGoals: 2.10.A Construct representations of the inverse of an exponential function with an initial value of 1.
lesson.bigIdea: The exponential function bˣ and the logarithmic function log_b x undo each other. Every fact about one becomes a fact about the other with inputs and outputs switched.
lesson.context: Topic 2.8 found inverses by reversing input-output pairs, and Topic 2.9 defined log_b c. Here the two meet: log_b x is the inverse function of bˣ.

sections.title: 2.10.A · The general form of a logarithmic function is f(x) = a log_b x.
sections.conceptTitle: General form of a logarithmic function

blocks.text: The general form of a logarithmic function is f(x) = a log_b x, with base b, where b > 0, b ≠ 1, and a ≠ 0.
Example: f(x) = 3 log₂ x has a = 3 and base 2. Then f(8) = 3 log₂ 8 = 3(3) = 9.

sections.takeaway: f(x) = a log_b x with b > 0, b ≠ 1, and a ≠ 0.

sections.title: 2.10.A · Exponential growth and logarithmic growth trade the roles of addition and multiplication.
sections.conceptTitle: How exponential and logarithmic change compare

blocks.text: The way in which input and output values vary together have an inverse relationship in exponential and logarithmic functions. Output values of general-form exponential functions change proportionally as input values increase in equal-length intervals. However, input values of general-form logarithmic functions change proportionally as output values increase in equal-length intervals. Alternately, exponential growth is characterized by output values changing multiplicatively as input values change additively, whereas logarithmic growth is characterized by output values changing additively as input values change multiplicatively.

blocks.caption: y = 2ˣ and y = log₂ x on the same values with roles switched

blocks.text: For 2ˣ, adding 1 to the input multiplies the output by 2. For log₂ x, multiplying the input by 2 adds 1 to the output.

sections.takeaway: Exponential: add to inputs, multiply outputs. Logarithmic: multiply inputs, add to outputs.

sections.title: 2.10.A · log_b x and bˣ are inverse functions.
sections.conceptTitle: Logarithmic and exponential functions as inverses

blocks.text: f(x) = log_b x and g(x) = bˣ, where b > 0 and b ≠ 1, are inverse functions. That is, g(f(x)) = f(g(x)) = x.

The graph of the logarithmic function f(x) = log_b x, where b > 0 and b ≠ 1, is a reflection of the graph of the exponential function g(x) = bˣ, where b > 0 and b ≠ 1, over the graph of the identity function h(x) = x.

blocks.caption: g(x) = 2ˣ and f(x) = log₂ x, reflections of each other over the line y = x
blocks.alt: An exponential curve g through (0, 1), (1, 2), and (2, 4), and a dashed logarithmic curve f through (1, 0), (2, 1), and (4, 2). A dashed gray line y = x lies between them, and each curve is the mirror image of the other across it.

blocks.text: If (s, t) is an ordered pair of the exponential function g(x) = bˣ, where b > 0 and b ≠ 1, then (t, s) is an ordered pair of the logarithmic function f(x) = log_b x, where b > 0 and b ≠ 1.

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam
blocks.text: Because (3, 125) is on the graph of y = 5ˣ, the point (125, 3) is on the graph of y = log₅ x, so log₅ 125 = 3.

sections.takeaway: Switch every ordered pair of bˣ to get log_b x; the graphs reflect over y = x.

connections.title: Inverses reverse pairs
connections.body: Topic 2.8 showed that an inverse function consists of the pairs (b, a) when the function consists of (a, b). log_b x is that construction applied to bˣ.
connections.transferQuestion: The graph of y = 4ˣ contains (1/2, 2). Which point is on y = log₄ x?

connections.title: Characteristics of logarithmic functions
connections.body: Topic 2.11 uses the reflection over y = x to read the domain, range, concavity, and vertical asymptote of a logarithmic function from those of an exponential function.
connections.transferQuestion: y = 2ˣ has the horizontal asymptote y = 0. What asymptote does y = log₂ x have?
connections.feedback: The vertical asymptote x = 0, the reflection of y = 0 over y = x.
